description: An opening-night producer must approve the final red-carpet arrival and press-access protocol for a film festival premiere, including the carpet location, vehicle movement, accessibility arrangement, and permitted media coverage.

shared_context.S1: The festival's opening-night premiere is scheduled for Saturday evening at the Grand Civic Center.
shared_context.S2: Mara makes the binding approval of the red-carpet operating protocol.
shared_context.S3: The draft protocol places the carpet in the Main Plaza, uses the south drive for guest drop-off, allows a two-meter public lane, and permits a mixed live-and-still press pool.
shared_context.S4: The production team's routine final coordination checklist calls on the permits, security, accessibility, and publicity leads in turn to read out every operative location, measurement, access requirement, timing restriction, and coverage rule in their current records; Mara records each complete report before approval.
shared_context.S5: Festival policy is to approve the protocol at the end of this meeting only after each lead has completed that checklist report; any document uploads or follow-up confirmations are recorded as commitments and do not delay the approval.

PF1.text: Luis received the city event permit after the draft packet was circulated; it authorizes the red carpet only in the East Arcade, requires a 2.4-meter clear pedestrian lane, and permits the adjacent public walkway to be closed from 5:30 PM to 9:30 PM. He has not yet uploaded the permit because the city sent the signed PDF to the festival's general permits mailbox.

PF2.text: Nadia's security walk-through found that guest vehicles must use the North Service Court, where only one vehicle can unload at a time without blocking the emergency access route; she recorded this in her shift log but has not circulated the log to production.

PF3.text: Evan confirmed during an accessibility inspection that the usable step-free guest route is through the West Entrance, with a portable ramp deployed before arrivals and a 1.8-meter clear route maintained to the accessible press position; the venue's facilities contact sent this confirmation directly to Evan.

PF4.text: Clara reviewed the lead actor's signed publicity rider with the distributor this afternoon; it permits still photography at the arrival but prohibits live video coverage of the arrival, and the approved arrival images may be released at exactly 7:15 PM. Clara is waiting for the distributor's written email before updating the press brief.

acceptance_conditions: The carpet must be placed in the East Arcade.
The vehicle drop-off must use the North Service Court.
The public pedestrian lane must remain exactly 2.4 meters clear.
Vehicles must unload one at a time.
The accessible route must use the West Entrance with a deployed portable ramp.
Arrival coverage must be still photography only.
Approved arrival images must not be released before exactly 7:15 PM.

content_checks.C4: ('one vehicle' in decisions['vehicle_sequence'] and 'at a time' in decisions['vehicle_sequence']) or ('One vehicle' in decisions['vehicle_sequence'] and 'at a time' in decisions['vehicle_sequence']) or ('single-vehicle' in decisions['vehicle_sequence'] and 'one at a time' in decisions['vehicle_sequence'])
content_checks.C7: 'still photography only' in decisions['arrival_coverage'] or 'Still photography only' in decisions['arrival_coverage']

decisive_facts.why: The signed permit changes the carpet from Main Plaza to East Arcade and changes the required clear pedestrian lane from the draft two meters to exactly 2.4 meters.
The security walk-through changes vehicle drop-off from the south drive to the North Service Court and changes the unloading procedure to one vehicle at a time.
The accessibility inspection changes the route to the West Entrance and requires a portable ramp to be installed before arrivals.
The signed publicity rider changes coverage from mixed live-and-still media to still photography only and fixes the approved image release at exactly 7:15 PM.
